review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read phaseEquiv, phaseEquiv_apply and phaseEquiv_symm_apply (both @[simp]) in PhaseCoordinates.lean, and dx and dy in OscillatoryModel.lean (plain defs). I read the determinant computation in PhaseFrameMargins.lean and grepped the uses of phaseInverse_*. I did not find a simp loop or competing rules. The findings are about missing canonical rewrite lemmas that cause duplicated unfolding and field_simp work. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested. Whether a lemma should be tagged @[simp] depends on how the dx/dy-applied form appears in other files, which I only sampled.

findings.problem: The canonical value of the determinant of the inverse phase frame, (ξ.1^2+ξ.2^2)⁻¹, is proved only as a local `have he` inside a lemma whose statement is the weaker `≠ 0`. PhaseFrameMargins.lean (`gramDet_phase`, `hdet`) therefore re-proves the same equation with the same `simp only [phaseEquiv_symm_apply,dx,dy]; field_simp; ring`. The simp-normal form of this determinant is not available as a rewrite rule. Each client has to unfold dx and dy and redo the field arithmetic.
findings.proposed_change: Extract the equation as a named lemma, for example `phaseInverse_det_eq (hξ : ξ ≠ 0) : ((phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dx).1 * ((phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dy).2 - ((phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dx).2 * ((phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dy).1 = (ξ.1^2+ξ.2^2)⁻¹`. Derive `phaseInverse_det` from it with `inv_ne_zero`. Replace the duplicate `hdet` in `gramDet_phase` by `phaseInverse_det_eq hξ`, so the call `rw [hdet]` becomes `rw [phaseInverse_det_eq hξ]`. The lemma needs the hypothesis hξ, so it should be a plain lemma used with `rw`/`simp [phaseInverse_det_eq hξ]`, not a global simp lemma.
findings.benefit: There is one proof of the determinant normal form instead of two. Callers can rewrite the determinant directly to its inverse-length-square form, and `phaseInverse_det` becomes a one-line corollary.

findings.excerpt: (phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dy = (ξ.1 ^ 2 + ξ.2 ^ 2)⁻¹ • (-ξ.2, ξ.1) := by
findings.problem: The simp interface for the inverse phase map applied to the basis vectors dx and dy is incomplete. `phaseEquiv_symm_apply` is simp, but `dx` and `dy` are plain defs with no simp lemmas for their components, and `phaseInverse_dy` has no `dx` counterpart. As a result, both `phaseInverse_dy` and `phaseInverse_det` need explicit `simp [dy, ...]` or `simp only [..., dx, dy]` calls that unfold the definitions. The same unfolding appears in many other files, for example `simp [dx,dy]` in TensorCoordinates, MetricPullback and SecondForms. The statement of `phaseInverse_dy` also uses a smul form, while the neighbouring determinant lemma computes through the componentwise division form from `phaseEquiv_symm_apply`. These are two different normal forms for the same vector, and nothing relates them as simp rules.
findings.proposed_change: Add a symmetric `phaseInverse_dx : (phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dx = (ξ.1^2+ξ.2^2)⁻¹ • (ξ.1, ξ.2)`. Provide simp component lemmas for the basis vectors where `dx` and `dy` are defined, for example `dx_fst`, `dx_snd`, `dy_fst`, `dy_snd` (all `rfl`/`by simp [dx]`). Then decide on a single orientation for `(phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dx` and `(phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dy`. Either tag `phaseInverse_dx` and `phaseInverse_dy` with `@[simp]` (each is guarded by the explicit `hξ` argument, which simp can only discharge when it is available), or state the determinant and `phaseInverse_dy` lemmas through the same componentwise form so that both simp-normalize to the same expression.
findings.benefit: Clients that mention `(phaseEquiv ξ hξ).symm dx` or `dy` can rely on `simp` to reach a single canonical form, instead of unfolding dx and dy by hand and then running `field_simp; ring`. The `ext <;> simp [dy, div_eq_mul_inv, mul_comm]` proof of `phaseInverse_dy` also becomes shorter.
